1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Sh. Gayaninder Singh vs Union Of India on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16443538/

08/200506/DC(NW)) Gayaninder Singh . v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar in possession of 1/12 share in the land bearing Khasra no. 39/14/2 (20), 17(416), 24(416) total land admeasuring 11 bigha 10 biswas situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).

5. It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been arbitrarily assessed by LAC no. 252 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Gayaninder Singh . v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 the LAC without taking into account the fertility,
potentiality, surroundings and topography under acquisition.

sentences.text: The said land is levelled land and is situated in a belt which has not experienced any major earthquake, flood or any other natural calamity for the last more than hundred years and is best suited for all sorts of land uses like residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural etc. the quality of the said land makes it most suitable in the state of Delhi.
6. It is stated that the said land falls in the most fertile belt of Delhi and the petitioners are cultivating the said land and are growing three crops in a year "fasali year".

Whole of the said land is having welldeveloped irrigation system having borwell, tubewells and canal system linked with Yamuna Canal and all crops including cereals, vegetables crops, oil yielding crops and sugarcane are being cultivated by the petitioners and the income per acre is more than Rs. 2 lakhs per year.
In addition to it, the petitioners are having milk yielding cattles which are fully fed by the land produce and all the daily needs of the petitioners are fulfilled by the said land.

7. It is stated that the petitioners shall be forced to change from one mode of life i.e. agro based lifestyle to modern lifestyle due to the acquisition of the said land and the new lifestyle has become more expensive and the daily inflation shall have an adverse economic effect on the petitioners who were selfreliant before acquisition of the said land.

9. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming market value of Rs. 2000/ per sq. yards or Rs. 1 crores per acre in addition to the said market value.
The petitioners have also claimed solatium @ 30% and additional amount @ 12% and further claim interest @ 9% and 15% as per the provisions of the Act.

submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 18.03.2004 and the said land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for Planned Development of Delhi.
Notice under Section 9 and 10 of the Act were issued to the land owners/interested persons inviting their claims in respect of the land.

Various factors were taken into account by the learned LAC while assessing the market value of the said land and, now the petitioners are claiming excessive and exorbitant enhancement of LAC no. 252 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Gayaninder Singh . v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 the land and structures.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land or superstructures which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under :  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
OPP 17.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by LAC no. 252 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Gayaninder Singh . v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
18.

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
19. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
20. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court
, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

21. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement LAC no. 252 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Gayaninder Singh . v.
Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
22. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.decision:
21. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement LAC no. 252 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Gayaninder Singh . v.
